costs.heading: Costs and expenses
costs.text:
For the three months ended December 31, 2024, and 2023 we incurred operating expenses of $251,666 and $120,965 respectively.

For the three months ended December 31, 2024 and 2023, cost of product sold increased to $10,116 from $913. This is a direct result of the increase in shipping costs in the three months ended December 31, 2024 as the Company transitioned from retail sales to direct to consumer offerings. Shipping and freight costs in the three months ended December 31, 2024 totaled $4,398 and costs of cookie production totaled $5,499 while the costs of product sold in December 31, 2023 was comprised solely of limited freight costs of $913.

For the three months ended December 31, 2024 and 2023, advertising and promotional expenses increased to $12,940 (2024) from $3,798 in advertising and promotion for the three months ended December 31, 2023. This increase is largely due to increased direct-to-consumer advertising and promotional efforts during the period.

For the three-month period ended December 31, 2024 and 2023, selling, general, and administrative expenses increased from $41,559 (2023) to $61,332 (2024).

nonop.heading: Other Income (Expense)
nonop.text: For the three months period ended December 31, 2024 and 2023, total other expenses totaled $243,081 as compared to $301,967. A major portion of these results are related to accounting treatment applied to financing costs and debt and the amortization of debt discount during the three months ended December 31, 2023. During the three months ended December 31, 2024 we recorded interest income of $29,643 with no comparable income for the three months ended December 31, 2023. During the three months period ended December 31, 2024 we had interest expenses on debt of $211,179 as compared to interest expenses of $61,596 as we increased our debt by way of loans and debentures. During the three months period ended December 31, 2024 we recorded $2,050 for interest expense related to financing costs and $59,495 as amortization of debt discounts as compared to $38,890 for interest expense on financing costs and $201,481 as amortization of debt discount for the three months ended December 31, 2023 as we applied an account treatment to these items in 2023.

net.heading: Net Loss
net.text: Our net loss in the three months ended December 31, 2024 was relatively consistent with our net loss for the three months ended December 31, 2023. Net loss at December 31, 2024 totaled $479,606 as compared to a net loss of $422,034 in the three months ended December 31, 2023. The largest component of the increase to our current period net loss was an increase in operating expenses from $120,965 (2023) to $251,666 (2024) mainly due to an increase in professional fees and general and administrative expenses in the three months ended December 31, 2024, offset by a decrease in other expense to $243,081 (2024) from $301,967 (2023) which was mainly the result of a reduction of amortization in debt discount for the three months ended December 31, 2023 offset by interest expense for debt increasing in the three months ended December 31, 2024.

sbc.heading: Stock-Based Compensation
sbc.text:
The Company accounts for stock-based compensation in accordance with ASC 718, “Compensation – Stock Compensation,” using the fair value-based method. Under this guidance, compensation cost is measured at the grant date based on the fair value of the award and is recognized over the requisite service period, typically the vesting period.

ASC 718 establishes accounting standards for transactions in which an entity exchanges its equity instruments for goods or services. It also applies to transactions where an entity incurs liabilities based on the fair value of its equity instruments or liabilities that may be settled using equity instruments.

The Company applies the fair value method for equity instruments granted to both employees and non-employees, aligning non-employee share-based payment accounting with that of employees.

tax.heading: Income Taxes
tax.text:
The Company accounts for income taxes using the asset and liability method prescribed by FASB ASC 740, Income Taxes. Under this method, deferred tax assets and liabilities are recognized for the expected future tax consequences of temporary differences between the financial reporting and tax bases of assets and liabilities. These deferred amounts are measured using enacted tax rates expected to apply in the periods when the temporary differences are expected to reverse.

The effect of a change in tax law or tax rates on deferred tax balances is recognized in the period in which the change is enacted.

All deferred tax assets and liabilities are presented as noncurrent in the Company’s consolidated balance sheet, regardless of the classification of the related asset or liability for financial reporting purposes.

C — Loss on debt extinguishment. Increased slightly by $2,225, to $(113,955) in fiscal 2025 from $(111,730) in fiscal 2024. In both years, this line item reflected one-time non-cash losses related to modifications and settlements of debt instruments.

D — Derivative expense. New non-cash charge of $(653,792) in fiscal 2025, compared to none in 2024. This arose from debt instruments acquired with SWC that became convertible upon closing on March 31, 2025, triggering recognition of an embedded derivative liability at fair value.

net.heading: Net Loss
net.text:
Net loss for the year ended June 30, 2025, was $8,115,878, compared to a net loss of $3,235,506 for the year ended June 30, 2024. This represents an increase in net loss of $4,880,372, or 151%.

The increase in net loss was primarily the result of:

The majority of the year-over-year increase in net loss reflects the Company’s strategic acquisitions of SWC and Foodservice Packaging and the integration of those businesses, coupled with acquisition-related financing structures. Many of these charges were non-cash and non-recurring in nature but were necessary to position the Company for future growth.

ocf.heading: Operating Activities
ocf.text: Net cash used in operating activities was $(1,634,483) in fiscal 2025, compared to $(709,990) in fiscal 2024, an increase in cash outflows of $924,493. The increase primarily reflects the higher net loss from continuing operations, partially offset by non-cash adjustments and changes in working capital accounts. Key year-over-year variances are discussed below.

da.heading: D. Depreciation and Amortization
da.text: Depreciation and amortization totaled $45,552 in fiscal 2025 compared to none in the prior year. The increase reflects the capitalization of property, equipment, and intangible assets acquired as part of the SWC acquisition, which support both the packaging and RaaS operations.

sbc.heading: Stock-Based Compensation
sbc.text:
The Company accounts for stock-based compensation in accordance with ASC 718, “Compensation – Stock Compensation,” using the fair value-based method. Under this guidance, compensation cost is measured at the grant date based on the fair value of the award and is recognized over the requisite service period, typically the vesting period.

ASC 718 establishes accounting standards for transactions in which an entity exchanges its equity instruments for goods or services. It also applies to transactions where an entity incurs liabilities based on the fair value of its equity instruments or liabilities that may be settled using equity instruments.

The Company applies the fair value method for equity instruments granted to both employees and non-employees, aligning non-employee share-based payment accounting with that of employees.

cor.text: Cost of sales was $2,807,691, compared to $412,503 in fiscal 2025, and consists of property-level operating costs at the hotels (payroll, utilities, guest supplies, food and beverage, and franchise, management and other property costs), product and fulfillment costs at SWC, and direct deployment costs in the RaaS segment. ga.heading: E. General and Administrative Expenses
ga.text: General and administrative expenses were $15,850,047, compared to $3,673,760 in fiscal 2025, an increase of $12,176,287, or 331%. Non-cash charges included in general and administrative expenses were $2,003,110 from the vesting of Series C Convertible Preferred Stock issued as compensation (fiscal 2025: $1,521,840), $439,608 of stock option expense on options granted during the year (fiscal 2025: none), $366,720 of stock issued for services, being $84,000 of common stock and $282,720 of Series C Convertible Preferred Stock (fiscal 2025: $98,195), $253,400 of common stock issued for intellectual property (fiscal 2025: none) and $58,769 of bad debt expense (fiscal 2025: $201,859). General and administrative expenses also include operating lease cost of $488,727 (fiscal 2025: none). The remaining increase reflects:

nonop.heading: Other Income (Expense) - net
nonop.text: Other expense, net, was $(7,040,347), compared to $(3,389,112) in fiscal 2025, an increase in net other expense of $3,651,235, or 108%. The increase reflects higher interest expense and amortization of debt discount on the mortgage notes assumed with the hotels and the convertible notes issued during the year, and higher derivative expense on the new convertible notes, partially offset by a non-cash gain on the change in fair value of derivative liabilities and the absence of the prior-year loss on settlement of pre-existing assets. Each line is discussed under “Other Income (Expense) - net” below.

ocf.text: Cash used in operating activities was $(8,051,852), compared to $(1,634,483) in fiscal 2025. The net loss from continuing operations of $(84,651,162) included non-cash charges of $63,886,000 for goodwill impairment, $3,194,106 of depreciation and amortization, $348,502 of amortization of the operating lease right-of-use asset, $3,279,129 of amortization of debt discount, $2,809,438 of stock-based compensation, $1,438,825 of derivative expense, $109,283 of loss on settlement of accounts payable - related party, $258,723 of commitment fee expense, $253,400 of stock issued for intellectual property, $58,769 of bad debt expense and $48,805 of interest added to debt, offset by the $1,007,680 gain on the change in fair value of derivative liabilities. Working capital provided $2,027,011, principally a $3,792,037 increase in accounts payable and accrued expenses due to related parties (accrued compensation and bonuses of officers and directors, accrued interest on related party notes and the related party line of credit and expenses paid on our behalf) and a $54,844 decrease in inventory, offset by a $1,076,645 decrease in trade accounts payable and accrued expenses, a $540,281 increase in prepaids and other and a $172,440 increase in accounts receivable. Discontinued operations used $105,001.

da.heading: D. Depreciation and Amortization
da.text: Depreciation and amortization was $3,194,106, compared to $45,552 in fiscal 2025. The increase reflects depreciation of the hotel buildings, land improvements and furniture, fixtures and equipment from the acquisition dates and amortization of the franchise, customer relationship and other intangible assets acquired with the hotels and SWC.

wc.heading: Working Capital
wc.text: Cash increased $515,658 to $865,889 at June 30, 2026, reflecting $7,876,420 of net financing proceeds and $1,269,000 of cash acquired with the hotels, offset by $8,051,852 of cash used in operating activities and $577,910 of capital expenditures. The increase in the working capital deficit of $19,073,224 reflects the current liabilities assumed or incurred with the acquired businesses and the financings described above, including the line of credit - related party of $3,392,000, the current portion of convertible notes payable of $6,688,967, notes payable of $5,198,020, derivative liabilities of $5,955,393 and accounts payable and accrued expenses of $8,919,654, including $4,060,420 due to related parties.

capex.text: Investing activities provided $691,090, consisting of $1,269,000 of cash acquired with the hotels, offset by $577,910 of purchases of property and equipment, principally robotics units and parts, hotel furniture, fixtures and equipment and renovation costs. The hotels themselves were acquired for Series C Convertible Preferred Stock and are non-cash investing activities. In fiscal 2025, investing activities used $(602,118), consisting of $429,607 of advances to acquisition targets and $200,851 of purchases of property and equipment, offset by $28,340 of cash acquired.
